title: Security & Compliance Controls, Evidence Workflows, RBAC and Risk Exceptions
author: Ava Chen
body:
Overview

This document consolidates Redwood Inference's operational controls and workflows for RBAC & authentication, audit logging, data residency & retention, secure SDLC gates, incident response for security events, compliance evidence collection, and the risk/exception process. It is intended for service owners, engineering leads, security engineers, and compliance partners.

Scope

- Applies to all Redwood-managed environments: hosted API, dedicated, and private deployments.
- Covers platform control plane, serving runtime, console, observability pipelines, and developer-facing APIs.
- Excludes third-party vendor internal controls; see supplier-security inventory for vendor-specific obligations.

1) RBAC & Authentication

Goal: Ensure least privilege access, traceable privilege elevation, and consistent identity lifecycle across cloud accounts and the Redwood control plane.

Key concepts and services
- Identity providers: Okta for SSO (SAML/OIDC), SCIM provisioning to Redwood IAM.
- Access control model: Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) with resource-scoped roles (project, org, customer).
- Short-lived service credentials: AWS STS for cloud infra; mTLS and short JWTs for internal service-to-service authentication.

Role definitions (examples)
- security-admin: full control over security configuration, audit access. Owner: Security Team.
- infra-operator: manage infra (deployments, scaling), no access to customer plaintext data. Owner: Eng-Infra.
- product-owner: configure product routes, feature flags. Owner: Product.
- svc-runtime: machine identity for serving runtime, scoped to GPU clusters. Owner: Eng-Serving-Runtime.

Provisioning and lifecycle
1. New hire/offboard flows provisioned via Okta + SCIM; access expires when Okta deactivates the user.
2. Role assignment requires an approval ticket in Jira with 2 approvers for privileged roles (security-admin, infra-operator).
3. Service accounts follow the least-privilege IAM policy; secrets rotated every 90 days or on key compromise.

Elevations and temporary access
- Just-in-time (JIT) access is available for emergency investigations via an approval workflow in Conjur/HashiCorp Vault with 4-hour timeboxes. All JIT grants are logged to audit (see Audit Logging).

Authentication policies and enforcement
- MFA: Required for all human access to production systems (Okta MFA).
- Passwords: Managed by SSO; no local passwords for critical systems.
- Service-to-service: mTLS with cert rotation managed by in-house PKI (rotation every 180 days).

2) Audit Logging

Objectives: Maintain an immutable, searchable record of security-relevant events for detection, investigations, and compliance evidence.

What to collect (minimum event set)
- Authentication events: logins, SSO token issuance, MFA successes/failures.
- Authorization events: role assignment, permission checks, policy denials.
- Privileged actions: RBAC role changes, IAM policy changes, key material creation/deletion.
- Admin operations: deployments, scaling changes, configuration rollouts to production.
- Data access: read/write access to customer data stores, object storage reads (logged with dataset and principal).
- Audit trail for JIT access and emergency access requests.

Ingestion and retention
- Primary pipeline: Events are sent to the centralized logging cluster and indexed in Splunk (or Datadog Log Management).
- Immutable storage bucket: WORM-enabled S3 bucket (us-east-1, us-west-2 as configured per region) for tamper-evident storage of raw events.
- Retention policy: Security-grade events retained for 7 years for enterprise customers where required; default company retention is 3 years for audit-critical events, 13 months for operational logs.

Alerting and monitoring
- Real-time SIEM correlation rules for brute force, privilege escalation, anomalous API usage (thresholds defined below).
- Threshold examples: >5 failed SSO auths from same account in 15 minutes => SEV-2 investigation; >3 privilege escalations in 1 hour => SEV-1 investigation.

Access to logs
- Security analysts and SREs have read access to indexed logs via role-based search views. Raw immutable bucket access restricted to security-admin and compliance roles.

3) Data Residency & Retention

Principles
- Customer data residency must be respected by deployment region selection (US, EU, APAC where supported).
- Metadata and telemetry required for operation are pseudonymized where feasible.
- Retention aligns with customer agreements and legal requirements.

Default retention for hosted API (examples)
- Short-term logs (request traces, ephemeral telemetry): 90 days.
- Indexed logs and audit events: 3 years (default) / up to 7 years for enterprise contracts.
- Model inputs/outputs (stored for debugging): retained for 30 days by default, configurable per-customer under contract.

Data residency controls and configuration table
| Data type | Default residency | Retention | Storage location | Owner |
|---|---:|---:|---|---|
| Audit logs | Multi-region (as required) | 3y / configurable | S3 (WORM) | Security |
| Customer embeddings | Region-bound | 30d / per-contract | Encrypted S3 in customer region | Product/Customer Support |
| Model KV cache snapshots | Multi-region | 14d | Encrypted object store | Eng-Serving-Runtime |

Customer choices and compliance notes
- For Private deployments, data never leaves customer VPC unless explicitly configured.
- Contracts must include residency clauses for regulated customers (HIPAA, GDPR data localization requirements).

4) Secure SDLC (Software Development Lifecycle)

Goal: Integrate security gates into the CI/CD pipeline and enforce secure-by-default practices.

Pre-commit and Build stage
- SCA (software composition analysis) to detect new vulnerable dependencies (blocker for CVEs with severity >= High for prod images).
- Linting, unit tests, and type checks required for all PRs.

Continuous Integration
- SAST scans on PRs; DAST scheduled on release branches.
- Dependency pinning and SBOM generated for each build artifact.
- Container image signing for all images that progress to staging.

Release & Production Promotion
- Promotion requires passing the security gate: SAST pass, SBOM reviewed, image signed, infra drift scan clean.
- Secrets detection (git-secrets/pre-commit hooks) enforced on push and monitored by pre-receive hooks.

Responsibilities and owners
- Devs: produce SBOM, address security findings in PRs.
- Security team: triage SAST results and maintain rule sets.
- Eng-Platform: maintain CI runners and SCA tooling.

5) Incident Response (Security) Procedures

Purpose: Provide a repeatable workflow for responding to security incidents affecting confidentiality, integrity, or availability.

Incident classification
- SEV-1: Active compromise of production customer data or control plane; immediate exec notification.
- SEV-2: Significant service degradation with security implications; security pager and on-call SRE involvement.
- SEV-3: Suspected reconnaissance, low-impact policy violations.

Response steps (high level)
1. Detection & Triage: Alerts come from SIEM, monitoring, or external reports. SOC/On-call assesses severity within 15 minutes.
2. Containment: Isolate affected services, revoke suspicious keys (short-lived tokens), and apply WAF rules.
3. Eradication: Remove compromised artifacts (images, keys), patch vulnerabilities.
4. Recovery: Restore from known-good images/snapshots; validate integrity checksums.
5. Post-incident review: Publish postmortem, remediation plan, and update runbooks.

Communication and escalation
- Pager duty routing: Security on-call -> Eng SRE -> Eng-Platform -> Execs.
- Customer notification: Follow SEC-PRIV disclosure timelines and templates; legal and customer-success coordinate notifications for customer-affecting incidents.

Forensic evidence preservation
- Preserve snapshots of relevant audit logs in immutable storage and image-level forensic copies. Document chain-of-custody in the incident ticket.

6) Compliance Evidence Workflows

Purpose: Define owners, artifacts, and timelines for producing evidence for audits (SOC2, ISO27001, GDPR).

Owners and artifacts
- Security (owner): Policies, control descriptions, SOC2 control mappings, penetration test summaries.
- Eng-Platform (owner): Infrastructure diagrams, change logs, access control lists, SRE runbooks.
- HR/People Ops: Background check records, training completion artifacts.

Evidence collection runbook (summary)
1. Audit intake: Compliance requests assigned a ticket in the compliance tracker with an initial 5 business day SLA to provide primary artifacts.
2. Evidence pull: Owners collect artifacts (PDFs, config exports, logs) and upload to the evidence repository (encrypted bucket).
3. Assertion & attestation: Security prepares control narratives and signs assertions.
4. External auditor access: Granted read-only access to a scoped evidence bundle; time-limited credentials issued via Okta.

Standard evidence artifacts list (examples)
- IAM role change logs (last 12 months)
- System configuration baselines and drift reports
- Pen test report (redacted) and remediation tickets
- Incident postmortems and SRM tickets for major security incidents

7) Risk & Exceptions Process

Principles
- Exceptions are time-limited, compensating controls must be defined, and high-risk exceptions require executive sign-off.

Exception request steps
1. Submit exception request in Jira (security-exceptions project) including: affected control, justification, compensating controls, risk impact, mitigations, requested duration.
2. Security triage: Security reviews within 3 business days and assigns a risk owner.
3. Approval matrix: Low risk -> Security approver; Medium risk -> Security + Eng lead; High risk -> Security + Eng lead + CTO/executive sponsor.
4. Monitoring: Approved exceptions are added to the risk register with monitoring criteria and expiry reminders.

Risk register table (example entries)
| Exception ID | Control impacted | Risk owner | Compensating controls | Expiry | Status |
| EXC-2024-001 | JIT access without logging to central SIEM (legacy) | Miguel Ortiz | Short-term packet capture, manual audit every 24 hours | 2024-12-01 | Remediated |
| EXC-2025-002 | Cross-region backup replication delay | Eng-Infra | Near-real-time integrity checks | 2025-03-01 | Approved |

Operational runbooks and links
- RBAC runbook: /confluence/security-and-compliance/rbac-runbook (procedural steps for role audits and periodic reviews).
- Incident playbook: /confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/incident-process (detailed playbooks and communications templates).
- Evidence repository: Internal secure bucket (s3://redwood-compliance-evidence) with access controlled via Okta group: compliance-auditors@redwood.com.

Appendices
A. Contact matrix
- Security triage (on-call): security-oncall@redwood.com (PagerDuty)
- Audit requests: compliance@redwood.com
- Legal: legal@redwood.com

B. Thresholds quick reference
- Failed SSO auths: >5 in 15 minutes => SEV-2
- Privilege escalations: >3 in 1 hour => SEV-1
- Unusual data egress spike: >2x baseline for customer dataset => immediate investigation

C. Change log
- 2024-08-15: Document created by Ava Chen.
- 2024-11-12: Added JIT access logging and SIEM thresholds (Miguel Ortiz).
- 2025-02-10: Updated retention policy and risk register examples (Priya Kapoor).

If you are an owner referenced in this document, ensure your operational runbooks and dashboards reflect the controls above and coordinate with security@redwood.com for quarterly audits and tabletop exercises.
